t: Moscow was a minor border town when it was first recorded in 1147, and it rose under Daniel's descendants, who collected tribute for the khan of the Golden Horde and drew the seat of the Russian Church to the city.

Ivan III united nearly all the Russian states with Moscow and rebuilt the Kremlin, and in 1547 Ivan the Terrible was crowned there as the first tsar of all Russia, but Peter the Great moved his government to Saint Petersburg in 1712.
Moscow became the capital again in 1918 under Lenin, grew through the Soviet period, held back the German army in 1941 and 1942, and remained the capital of the Russian Federation after 1991.
dyk: In 1937 letters were written to the Central Committee of the Communist Party proposing that Moscow be renamed "Stalindar" or "Stalinodar". Stalin rejected the suggestion.
ev: Moscow is first mentioned in the chronicles, as a meeting place of two princes
The Mongols burn the city during their invasion of Rus
The foundation of the Dormition Cathedral, the first stone church of Moscow, is laid
Dmitry Donskoy leads a united Russian army to victory over the Mongols at Kulikovo
The Zemsky Sobor elects Michael Romanov as tsar
Napoleon's army occupies Moscow, and a fire ruins much of the city
Lenin moves the capital back to Moscow on 12 March

f.founded: First documented in 1147, as a meeting place of Yuri Dolgorukiy and Sviatoslav Olgovich. Its first prince was Daniel, a son of Alexander Nevsky, who received it as hereditary land in 1263.
f.where: On the banks of the Moskva River on the East European Plain in Central Russia, in the present-day Russian Federation.
f.known: The Kremlin and Red Square; the rise of Muscovy under Ivan III; the doctrine of Moscow as the Third Rome; the burning of the city by the Crimean Tatars in 1571; the fire of 1812; capital of the Soviet Union; the Moscow Metro; the Battle of Moscow
f.today: Moscow is the capital and largest city of the Russian Federation and is governed as a federal city.
